title: Switch policy and label independently
frozenQuestion: After a state-matched mid-trajectory intervention, does subsequent spatial organization track the newly executable policy partition more than the retained pre-switch analysis-label partition, while changing only analysis labels leaves transitions unchanged?

scope.sourceConditions: The six balanced 50/50 pairwise, absent policy-value-association S06/S08 anchors: all three policy pairs on unique_1_100 and repeated_1_10_x10 inputs.

analysisLabels.originalCohort: The executable policy carried by each identity immediately before intervention; frozen before any S09 outcome.
analysisLabels.switchedCohort: The exact orthogonal policy assignment defined below, also used for the label-only intervention.
analysisLabels.activeAnalysisLabel: originalCohort unless labels are switched, then switchedCohort. This field is metadata only and never available to policy code.
analysisLabels.fixedGroupingRule: Both originalCohort and switchedCohort adjacency are measured in every arm, regardless of active label, so a grouping redefinition cannot masquerade as a behavioral effect.

interventionAssignment.eligibility: Exactly two executable policies with 50 identities each.
interventionAssignment.ordering: Within each original policy, rank cell IDs by SHA-256 of the S09 namespace, source runtime scenario ID, policy, and cell ID.
interventionAssignment.exchange: Retain the first 25 identities in each original policy and exchange executable policy for the remaining 25 in each group. Pair exchanged identities by within-policy SHA rank for donor-memory sensitivity.
interventionAssignment.crossTab: Each original-policy by switched-policy cell is exactly 25; original and switched binary partitions are orthogonal and each switched policy count remains exactly 50.
interventionAssignment.reason: Exchanging every identity in a balanced binary mixture is only a global name inversion and preserves the unlabeled partition. The orthogonal exact exchange creates a nontrivial, composition-preserving intervention.

timing.checkpointBoundary: Intervene immediately after the accepted swap whose one-based count equals floor(progress times the source scenario's validated native final successful-swap count), and before the next activation.
timing.peakDefinition: Earliest progress grid point attaining the condition-mean observed corrected-policy-adjacency maximum in the validated S06 observed_dynamic_trajectories.parquet; this upstream-only rule is frozen before S09 outcomes.
timing.terminalPeakRule: A peak checkpoint at progress 1.00 is executed and audited but has no post-switch exposure and is excluded from the primary kinetic success gate.

arms.role: primary policy intervention with retained labels

selectionInternalState.primaryRule: retain_old_reset_new: an identity that executes Selection both before and after intervention retains its own current cursor; an identity newly assigned Selection resets to the ascending boundary cursor 0; cursors are removed from identities no longer executing Selection.
selectionInternalState.sensitivityRule: donor_transfer: each post-switch Selection identity receives the checkpoint cursor of the original Selection donor whose policy assignment it receives; unchanged identities are their own donor. Cursors are removed from identities no longer executing Selection.
selectionInternalState.nonSelectionPairs: For Bubble+Insertion, the two rules are structurally identical and must replay exactly.
selectionInternalState.interpretation: The primary rule treats Selection memory as identity-local learned state; the sensitivity treats it as policy-instance state transferred with the executable policy.

stateAndRuntime.allowedPolicyArmChange: Executable policy and the explicitly prespecified Selection cursor map only.
stateAndRuntime.runtimeKey: Every arm retains the source runtime seed and source scenario_id. A modified Scenario is structurally validated under its content-addressed ID, then the S08 fixture restores the source scenario_id before continuation.
stateAndRuntime.schedulerCoupling: Global activation_count continues without reset. Actor draws are therefore address-identical across arms at every common global event index. Bubble-side draws are also address-identical whenever the selected actor executes Bubble in the compared arms; policy switching can change whether that stream is queried, so stream consumption after policy divergence is audited rather than required to remain equal.
stateAndRuntime.comparisonClock: Primary paired curves use 101 points on common post-checkpoint activation exposure through the maximum paired terminal exposure; completed or quiescent arms are carried forward as absorbing states. Accepted-swap counts are retained as a sensitivity descriptor, not used to recouple schedulers.

metricsAndEstimands.correctedAdjacency: same-label open-path edges divided by n=100 minus sum_k n_k(n_k-1)/n^2; both balanced partitions use 0.49.
metricsAndEstimands.partitionContrast: D = corrected adjacency of switchedCohort minus corrected adjacency of originalCohort.
metricsAndEstimands.policyTrackingCurve: [D(policy_only_primary,t)-D(policy_only_primary,checkpoint)] - [D(no_switch,t)-D(no_switch,checkpoint)]. Positive values mean post-switch dynamics favor the newly executable partition over the retained-label partition beyond the matched native continuation.
metricsAndEstimands.peak: maximum of the complete 101-point condition-mean policyTrackingCurve.
metricsAndEstimands.positiveArea: piecewise-linear integral of the positive part of the complete condition-mean policyTrackingCurve over common normalized activation exposure.
metricsAndEstimands.labelBehaviorEffect: For both fixed partitions and every state/transition field, label_only minus no_switch; required to be exactly zero.
metricsAndEstimands.activeLabelRegrouping: active-label corrected adjacency under label_only minus no_switch. This is reported as a grouping-definition contrast, not a transition effect.
metricsAndEstimands.factorialChecks: sham equals no_switch; both_primary equals policy_only_primary; both_transfer equals policy_only_transfer.
metricsAndEstimands.uncertainty: Ten-thousand stratified paired bootstrap resamples of scenario ordinals within condition; percentile 95% intervals. One-sided bootstrap p-values for positive policy tracking are Benjamini-Hochberg adjusted across condition by timing and outcome.
metricsAndEstimands.multiplicity: Condition-level inferential rows use BH q-values across the six conditions separately within Selection rule, timing, and outcome; terminal-progress rows are descriptive. Pooled success gates use prespecified stratified bootstrap intervals and are not selected from the condition tests.

successCriteria.validity: All 150 native sources replay the S07 final activation count, swap count, stop reason, and final state hash; every checkpoint is exact; all assignments have 25-per-cross-cell and 50/50 marginals; required state fields and runtime keys are preserved; no_switch equals sham, label_only equals no_switch, and each both arm equals its policy-only arm exactly; Selection cursors obey their frozen rule; policy code remains analysis-label-blind; S01-S08 are byte-immutable; S10 is absent; and accounting is complete.
successCriteria.policyTracking: At either the 25% or 50% timing, the pooled primary-rule peak and positive-area bootstrap lower bounds are both greater than zero and at least four of six condition-level point estimates are positive for both outcomes.
successCriteria.labelNull: All fixed-partition trajectories and terminal transition summaries are exactly identical between label_only and no_switch; active-label regrouping is explicitly separated from behavioral effects.
successCriteria.memoryRobustness: The donor-transfer sensitivity is reported for every Selection-containing condition; disagreement with the primary rule constrains interpretation but does not invalidate a correctly executed primary intervention.
successCriteria.supportive: Validity, policyTracking, and labelNull all pass.
successCriteria.null: Validity and labelNull pass but policyTracking does not, without a precise directional reversal.
successCriteria.constrainingOrContradictory: Any validity or labelNull gate fails, or primary policy tracking is precisely negative; Selection-rule sensitivity can additionally constrain the scope of a supportive primary result.

claimBoundaries: The policy intervention is randomized only through a prespecified deterministic assignment conditional on the frozen simulator scenarios; causal language is bounded to these state-matched simulator continuations.
Switching executable policy changes future local decision rules but not values, occupancy, scheduler addresses, or prior history.
Switching analysis labels changes a grouping definition and cannot by itself be interpreted as a behavioral treatment.
Completion fixes the unique-value order, so transient peak and positive area—not terminal aggregation—are primary.
A terminal upstream peak provides no post-switch kinetic exposure and is descriptive only.
S09 does not perform de-clustering, prove an attractor, or start S10.
